title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 1 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 1 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: By the time the examination begins tomorrow, the students ______ their revision for at least six hours.
questions.explanation: The sentence emphasizes the duration of an activity continuing up to a future point, so Future Perfect Continuous is required.

questions.questionText: When I reached the station, the train ______ already ______.
questions.explanation: The train left before another past event, so Past Perfect is used.

questions.questionText: She looks exhausted because she ______ since early morning.
questions.explanation: The activity began in the past and has continued recently, with emphasis on duration and present evidence.

questions.questionText: By next September, Dawit ______ at the university for four years.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'for four years' emphasizes duration up to a future point, requiring Future Perfect Continuous.

questions.questionText: I cannot open the door because I ______ my keys.
questions.explanation: The past action has a present result: the keys are unavailable now.

questions.questionText: The lecturer usually ______ at eight, but this week she ______ at nine because of the new schedule.
questions.explanation: The first is a regular habit, while the second describes a temporary current arrangement.

questions.questionText: While the researchers ______ the experiment, the electricity suddenly went off.
questions.explanation: The experiment was in progress when a shorter past event interrupted it.

questions.questionText: She ______ three chapters so far, but she ______ the final chapter yet.
questions.explanation: 'So far' and 'yet' connect unfinished actions with the present, so Present Perfect is appropriate.

questions.questionText: At this time next Monday, we ______ for our final examination.
questions.explanation: An activity in progress at a specific future time requires Future Continuous.

questions.questionText: He ______ in Addis Ababa for ten years before he moved to Bahir Dar.
questions.explanation: The activity continued for a duration before another past event, so Past Perfect Continuous is required.

questions.questionText: If you ______ metal sufficiently, it expands.
questions.explanation: This is a general scientific truth expressed with the Zero Conditional: Present Simple in both clauses.

questions.questionText: If she ______ harder last semester, she would have passed the examination.
questions.explanation: The Third Conditional uses Past Perfect in the if-clause.

questions.questionText: If I ______ enough money now, I would buy a new laptop.
questions.explanation: This describes an unreal present situation, so the Second Conditional uses Past Simple.

questions.questionText: If he had accepted the scholarship, he ______ at university now.
questions.explanation: A past condition produces a present result, forming a mixed conditional.

questions.questionText: The manager ______ the report yet, so we cannot send it to the client.
questions.explanation: The action remains unfinished and affects the present, so Present Perfect is needed.

questions.questionText: When the teacher entered, the students ______ quietly for several minutes.
questions.explanation: The waiting continued for a period before another past event.

questions.questionText: She ______ the same company since she graduated from university.
questions.explanation: 'Since she graduated' gives a starting point extending to the present, so Present Perfect is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Look at those clouds! It ______ rain heavily.
questions.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence uses 'be going to'.

questions.questionText: The telephone is ringing. I ______ it.
questions.explanation: A decision made at the moment of speaking commonly uses Future Simple with 'will'.

questions.questionText: We ______ the principal tomorrow because an appointment has already been arranged.
questions.explanation: A definite personal arrangement is expressed with Present Continuous for the future.

questions.questionText: The examination ______ at exactly 9:00 a.m. next Monday.
questions.explanation: An official timetable or fixed schedule uses Present Simple.

questions.questionText: I ______ him since 2018, so I know exactly how he thinks.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is normally a stative verb and is not normally used in continuous forms.

questions.questionText: She ______ about the problem at the moment, so do not interrupt her.
questions.explanation: 'Think' can be continuous when it means an ongoing mental activity.

questions.questionText: I ______ this book three times, and I still discover something new each time.
questions.explanation: Repeated experience up to the present uses Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: By the time you arrive, we ______ dinner.
questions.explanation: The dinner will be completed before a specified future event.

questions.questionText: By the end of this month, she ______ on the project for exactly six months.
questions.explanation: The emphasis is on the duration of the activity up to a future point.

questions.questionText: He ______ his assignment when the computer suddenly stopped working.
questions.explanation: The typing was in progress when another past event interrupted it.

questions.questionText: After the students ______ the examination, they left the classroom.
questions.explanation: The examination was completed before the students left, so Past Perfect emphasizes the earlier event.

questions.questionText: She ______ the report before the director asked for it.
questions.explanation: The report was completed before another past event.

questions.questionText: They ______ for more than an hour when the bus finally arrived.
questions.explanation: Duration before a past event requires Past Perfect Continuous.

questions.questionText: I ______ my assignment yesterday, so I can relax today.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so Past Simple is required.

questions.questionText: She ______ to Nairobi in 2022.
questions.explanation: A definite finished past time requires Past Simple.

questions.questionText: I ______ to Nairobi several times, but I have never lived there.
questions.explanation: Repeated life experience without a finished-time expression uses Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: How long ______ you ______ for this company?
questions.explanation: The question asks about a situation continuing from the past to the present.

questions.questionText: How long ______ you ______ before the manager finally arrived?
questions.explanation: The duration occurred before a past reference point, so Past Perfect Continuous is appropriate.

questions.questionText: When I was young, I ______ visit my grandparents every summer.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' expresses a repeated past habit.

questions.questionText: Every summer when we were children, we ______ swim in the river near our village.
questions.explanation: 'Would' can describe repeated past actions in a narrative context.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly describes a past state that is no longer true?
options: I used to live in Gondar.
I was living in Gondar every childhood.
I have lived in Gondar yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' can describe past states, whereas 'would' normally describes repeated actions.

questions.questionText: I will call you as soon as I ______ home.
questions.explanation: Future time clauses with 'as soon as' normally use Present Simple.

questions.questionText: We will not leave until the teacher ______ us permission.
questions.explanation: 'Until' introduces a future time clause, which normally uses Present Simple.

questions.questionText: Before you ______ the application, check all the information carefully.
questions.explanation: A future time clause introduced by 'before' takes Present Simple.

questions.questionText: She ______ the instructions carefully before she began the experiment.
questions.explanation: Reading occurred before another past event, so Past Perfect is suitable.

questions.questionText: While I ______ the report, my colleague ______ the data.
questions.explanation: Two activities were happening simultaneously in the past, so Past Continuous is used for both.

questions.questionText: As the students ______ into the classroom, the teacher was arranging the desks.
questions.explanation: 'As' introduces an activity occurring at the same time as another ongoing past activity.

questions.questionText: The company ______ rapidly these days because demand is increasing.
questions.explanation: 'These days' indicates a developing situation around the present.

questions.questionText: He ______ always ______ his phone whenever we need to contact him.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous with 'always' can emphasize repeated irritating behavior.

questions.questionText: She normally ______ coffee, but today she ______ tea.
questions.explanation: The first describes a habit; the second describes a temporary action today.

questions.questionText: The Earth ______ around the Sun.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact is expressed using Present Simple.

questions.questionText: The professor ______ the answer, but she is explaining it to the students now.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and normally remains in Present Simple.

questions.questionText: I ______ lunch at the moment, so I cannot answer the phone.
questions.explanation: 'Have' can be continuous when it means an activity such as eating lunch.

questions.questionText: She ______ a large house near the university.
questions.explanation: 'Own' is a stative verb and is normally used in Simple forms.

questions.questionText: I ______ the meaning of this sentence. Could you explain it?
questions.explanation: 'Understand' is normally stative and is not generally used in the continuous form.

questions.questionText: He ______ the answer now because he ______ about the problem for several hours.
questions.explanation: 'Understand' is stative, while 'think' can be continuous when referring to an ongoing mental activity.

questions.questionText: She ______ here since January, but she plans to move next month.
questions.explanation: The situation began in the past and continues to the present, so Present Perfect is appropriate.

questions.questionText: I ______ for three hours, and I still have not finished the assignment.
questions.explanation: The sentence emphasizes an ongoing activity and its duration up to the present.

questions.questionText: She ______ five pages since breakfast.
questions.explanation: The number of completed pages emphasizes result and quantity, favoring Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: She ______ since breakfast and has now finished five pages.
questions.explanation: The emphasis is on the ongoing activity from breakfast until now.

questions.questionText: By 2030, scientists ______ several new methods of producing clean energy.
questions.explanation: The sentence emphasizes completion before a future deadline.

questions.questionText: By 2030, scientists ______ clean-energy technology for decades.
questions.explanation: The focus is on the duration of development up to a future point.

questions.questionText: At 10 p.m. tonight, I ______ for my examination.
questions.explanation: The activity will be in progress at a specified future time.

questions.questionText: Do not call me at 7 p.m. because I ______ dinner with my family.
questions.explanation: Future Continuous describes an activity that will be in progress at a future time.

questions.questionText: Will you ______ the computer this evening?
questions.explanation: Future Continuous can be used for a polite question about someone's plans.

questions.questionText: By the time the semester ends, we ______ all twelve units.
questions.explanation: Completion before a future reference point requires Future Perfect.

questions.questionText: By the time the semester ends, we ______ English for nearly a year.
questions.explanation: The sentence emphasizes the duration of the activity leading to a future point.

questions.questionText: She ______ her homework before she went to bed.
questions.explanation: The homework was completed before another past action.

questions.questionText: When the police arrived, the crowd ______ outside the building for nearly an hour.
questions.explanation: The waiting continued for a duration before the police arrived.

questions.questionText: He ______ the office when I called him yesterday.
questions.explanation: The leaving was in progress around the time of the call, so Past Continuous is appropriate.

questions.questionText: When I called her yesterday, she ______ already ______ home.
questions.explanation: Her departure happened before the past phone call, requiring Past Perfect.

questions.questionText: He ______ the report when the manager entered, so he stopped typing.
questions.explanation: The writing was in progress when the manager entered.

questions.questionText: I ______ the report before the manager entered, so I was free to leave.
questions.explanation: The report was already completed before another past event.

questions.questionText: She ______ English for two years before she moved abroad.
questions.explanation: Duration of an activity before another past event requires Past Perfect Continuous.

questions.questionText: He ______ English for two years before he took the examination.
questions.explanation: The activity continued for a period before a past reference point.

questions.questionText: I ______ this problem several times, but I still cannot solve it.
questions.explanation: Repeated attempts connected to the present use Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: I ______ this problem yesterday, but I could not solve it.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, requiring Past Simple.

questions.questionText: She ______ never ______ such a difficult examination before.
questions.explanation: Life experience up to the present uses Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: Before that examination, she ______ never ______ such a difficult test.
questions.explanation: The experience occurred before a past reference point, so Past Perfect is required.

questions.questionText: This is the most difficult English examination I ______ ever ______.
questions.explanation: Superlatives referring to experience up to the present commonly use Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: That was the most difficult examination I ______ ever ______ at that time.
questions.explanation: The experience occurred before a past reference point, so Past Perfect is appropriate.

questions.questionText: She says that she ______ tired.
questions.explanation: With a present reporting verb, the original present tense normally remains unchanged.

questions.questionText: She said that she ______ tired.
questions.explanation: A past reporting verb commonly causes Present Simple to backshift to Past Simple.

questions.questionText: He said, "I am studying for the examination." Which is the correct reported form?
options: He said that he is studying for the examination.
He said that he was studying for the examination.
He said that he had studied for the examination.
He said that he has studied for the examination.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous normally backshifts to Past Continuous after a past reporting verb.

questions.questionText: She said, "I have finished the assignment." Which reported sentence is correct?
options: She said that she has finished the assignment.
She said that she finished the assignment.
She said that she had finished the assignment.
She said that she was finishing the assignment.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect normally changes to Past Perfect after a past reporting verb.

questions.questionText: He said, "I went home early." Which reported form follows the normal backshift rule?
options: He said that he goes home early.
He said that he had gone home early.
He said that he has gone home early.
He said that he was going home early.
questions.explanation: Past Simple normally backshifts to Past Perfect in reported speech.

questions.questionText: She said, "I will call you tomorrow." Which is the normal reported form?
options: She said that she will call me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she had called me the next day.
She said that she was calling me tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will normally backshifts to would in reported speech.

questions.questionText: The teacher said that water ______ at 100°C.
questions.explanation: A universal scientific truth can remain in Present Simple even after a past reporting verb.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Does she works at the university?
Does she work at the university?
Does she worked at the university?
Does she working at the university?
questions.explanation: After 'does', the main verb must be in its base form.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Did he went to school yesterday?
Did he goes to school yesterday?
Did he go to school yesterday?
Did he going to school yesterday?
questions.explanation: After 'did', the main verb must be V1.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses an action happening now?
questions.explanation: An action happening at the moment uses Present Continuous.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a completed action at a definite past time?
options: I have finished the work yesterday.
I had finished the work yesterday.
I was finishing the work yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past-time expression, so Past Simple is required.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses duration continuing to the present?
questions.explanation: 'Since 2020' gives a starting point extending to the present, requiring Present Perfect.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'for'?
options: I have lived here since five years.
I have lived here for five years.
I lived here for since five years.
questions.explanation: 'For' introduces a duration, while 'since' introduces a starting point.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'since'?
options: She has worked here since three years.
She worked here since three years.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is followed by a starting point such as a year.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains the correct tense sequence?
options: When I will arrive, I will call you.
When I arrive, I will call you.
When I arrived, I will call you.
When I am arrive, I will call you.
questions.explanation: A future time clause introduced by 'when' uses Present Simple.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly describes an official future timetable?
options: The train is leaving at 7 according to the official timetable.
The train leaves at 7 according to the official timetable.
The train has left at 7 tomorrow.
The train was leaving at 7 tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Present Simple is used for fixed timetables and official schedules.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best expresses a definite personal arrangement?
options: I am meeting my doctor tomorrow.
I have met my doctor tomorrow.
I was meeting my doctor tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous is commonly used for definite personal arrangements.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best expresses an intention already decided before speaking?
options: I am going to study tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' commonly expresses a prior intention or plan.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best expresses a spontaneous decision?
options: I am going to answer the phone.
I am answering the phone tomorrow.
questions.explanation: A decision made at the moment of speaking commonly uses 'will'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a prediction based on present evidence?
options: The sky is dark; it will have rained.
The sky is dark; it is going to rain.
The sky is dark; it rains.
The sky is dark; it has rained tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Present evidence supporting a future prediction commonly takes 'going to'.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a future action in progress?
options: At 6 tomorrow, I will be studying.
questions.explanation: Future Continuous expresses an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses completion before a future deadline?
options: By Friday, I will finish the project.
By Friday, I will have finished the project.
By Friday, I am finishing the project yesterday.
By Friday, I have finished the project.
questions.explanation: Future Perfect emphasizes completion before a future deadline.
